prompts.name: 01-houtrust
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: high-resolution blue-and-white architectural wall artwork, background only.
Output: one 3840 x 2160 pixel landscape image, 16:9, highest supported resolution and maximum fine detail. Artwork only: no website, no mockup, no UI, no cards, no players, no people, no compositing frames.
STYLE reference is input image 1, the existing club wall. Match its chalk-white rough plaster wall, realistic fine cracks, distressed screenprint blue ink architectural rendering, expressive broad dry-brush diagonal strokes, worn halftone and scattered ink flecks. Use a SINGLE deep club ink BLUE #03438A and chalk WHITE only; lighter marks are the same blue thinned through weathered white, not extra colors. Let structure remain crisp and recognizable within the weathering. Keep white breathing room around architectural outlines. No black, no colored photography.
COMPOSITION: Wide panoramic wall, naturally integrated faded stencil-like landmarks. Primary landmark wholly inside the LEFT x4%-40% portion, centered near x22%, prominent and legible for a mobile crop of x0%-45%. Landmark roof/top and base must remain complete inside the image. Keep its natural architectural proportions, never stretch it vertically. Broad region for this left scene is y26%-89%. Secondary landmark wholly in RIGHT x75%-98%, complete. Middle x45%-72% must remain an uninterrupted light/quiet chalk-white plaster zone for later copy and cards; no architecture, dense ink, or bold marks there. Give edges expressive blue drybrush energy without allowing brushwork to obliterate the landmarks. No collage panels, frames, borders, or giant words.
FIDELITY: Architectural photos are authoritative. Transcribe their actual physical geometry closely and consistently: proportions, outlines, roof shapes, windows, arches/openings, material joints and distinctive hardware. Change palette and medium, not the buildings. Do not reuse the inaccurate generic gatehouse or lighthouse depicted in input 1, which is STYLE ONLY. No invented substitute Dutch buildings. No slogan typography.
Input roles: image 1 = wall STYLE only; image 2 = canteen full structural view; image 3 = canteen close structural detail; image 4 = canteen windows/fascia perspective detail; image 5 = actual open entrance gate, authoritative secondary geometry.
SCENE 'Houtrust': Left main subject is the ACTUAL Duindorp S.V. canteen from images 2-4. Render the whole low, single-storey flat-roof canteen facade: rectangular exposed brick left end, long straight white horizontal ribbed fascia, one deep-blue horizontal stripe flanking the central sign, the accurate shield sign at its left and physical sign text exactly "DUINDORP S.V.", repeated dark glazed window and door bays underneath with blue slender vertical mullions, full low metal terrace railing in front, simple ground/base. Keep its distinctive long, low flat silhouette, continuous fascia, window rhythm and left brick pier; slight front three-quarter view based on image 2. No people, DJ, balloons, foreground advertisements or event furniture. Building occupies most of the left 4%-40% width yet its sign is only normal physical building-sign scale.
Right secondary is the ACTUAL simple metal open entrance gate from image 5: a long shallow rectangular horizontal overhead welcome board carried by tall narrow metal posts, three tall rectangular metal doors all opened, showing the empty pathways through them. Follow the photographed open-door angles, panel forms and post spacing. Physical board lettering exactly "WELKOM BIJ DUINDORP S.V." kept small and integral to gate. No masonry arch, no gatehouse, no peaked roof, no ornate iron gates. Use subtle blue ink tree suggestions behind these two structures, largely faded to white. This is one integrated wall mural, not a photo collage.

SCENE 'De wijk': Left main subject is exactly the Meeuwenhof arch from image 2, as a large faithful architectural screenprint in blue ink. A STRAIGHT broad brick residential facade with one broad rounded central passage opening, exactly TWO smaller narrow rounded arched doorways symmetrically flanking it, and rectangular white-framed multi-pane residential windows outside those doors. The huge central arch is about three times a small doorway's width, with very thick brick arch surround; through it the second receding arch and distant courtyard opening are plainly visible. Preserve photograph-based spatial depth, lintels, brickwork and asymmetric small plaques/pipes. Above, keep the straight horizontal residential facade and the partial upper-storey window detail from the photo, with a soft weathered fade into white plaster; DO NOT invent a pitched roof, triangular gable, gatehouse, turret, clock or new roof silhouette. Keep the entire main opening, side doors, windows and ground line visible within left x4%-40%. Leave white clear space around this architecture so that its outline stands apart from the background grunge.
Right secondary is the actual brick church from image 3, with its silhouette traced closely: tall narrow rectangular brick clock tower with its simple triangular saddle roof, dark horizontal louver openings high on BOTH visible faces, square clock faces directly beneath, tower positioned behind and to the right of the main nave as in the photo. The main nave has a steep large gable with small circular vent pattern high up, a rectangular front window lower down, and the characteristic series of small low zigzag porch gables across its lower front plus the repeated side gables. Preserve exact relative nave/tower heights and roof slopes. Whole church, cap and base completely visible in right x75%-98%. Minimize trees to prevent obscuring key architecture. No invented spire, cross, gothic windows, decorative domes or substitute church. No headline text anywhere.

SCENE 'Aan zee': Left main subject is the precise SHORT BROAD harbor lighthouse in images 2 and 3. It is a stout white cylindrical/faceted tower, with visible vertical panel seams, ONE thick blue horizontal middle stripe and a blue base band, a simple rectangular lower door, and small vent near the top. Tower body from base to gallery is only about 1.6 times its diameter. Gallery is a VERY WIDE flared open circular metal basket: its upper rim approximately 1.5 times tower-body width, flaring outward upward, supported by visible diagonal rods and open mesh panels; it is not a normal narrow horizontal balcony. Above is the thin-bar glass lamp canopy, visible lamp in center, with a simple LOW pointed cap and tiny central finial, exactly as photos. Total tower including lamp/cap about 2.4 times body diameter, never a skinny tall conventional lighthouse. Use the source's true stripe thickness, door location, gallery angles and cap shape; convert green to #03438A. Primary landmark in left x4%-40%, centered x22%, top around y26%-31% and full base around y79%. Beneath it put the source's concrete ANGULAR WAVE-BREAK CUBES and foaming waves, down to y89%; no rounded rocks. Enough white around lighthouse edges to clearly show the distinctive broad gallery and short body. No people, boats, fishing gear or captions.
Right secondary is a subtle lighter weathered blue aerial depiction of the actual Duindorp neighborhood in image 4, wholly in x75%-98%, roughly y42%-87%. Closely preserve its bird's-eye perspective, the strong straight central street running from near front toward the distant harbor, the curved near-front building-block corners on both sides of the street, long parallel repeated rows of flat-roof housing, dunes and sea toward the aerial view's left side, dense blocks to its right and the distant harbor/coastline. Do not replace it with generic old Dutch gabled canal houses. The aerial is a faded screenprint integrated behind/right blue brushwork but its street axis and block rhythm remain legible. Middle x45%-72% stays clear white. No text or watermarks.
